rendered:
The review does not say that DRX cathodes are already produced at scale by coprecipitation; it says the opposite. It states that DRX materials are generally made in gram-scale batches by energy-intensive mechanochemical and solid-state methods, as in the words DRX materials are generally synthesized in gram-scale[1] (with the rest of the sentence on the next line). It then calls for more scalable routes, in the words scalable routes (e.g., coprecipitation) are needed[2]. So coprecipitation is named there as a future route that DRX cathodes still need to be assessed against, not as an existing route.

The review does call coprecipitation a commercially viable method, but it makes that claim for cathodes in general, not for DRX specifically, in the words Coprecipitation is a commercially viable method[3]. Those statements do not extend to DRX cathodes, which the review treats as not yet scaled up.
